chapter: Joining Earl Hines and the Grand Terrace
title: Who was in the Hines band
summary: Rundown of brass, trombone and sax players, with George Dixon doubling.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: What was the band like? Who was in the band, do you recall some of the guys that you remember? In '31.
That's right, he was there. He was there with his wife. That's right. Him and Hilliard sat together.
You have George Dixon -- in the brass section we had George Dixon, Charlie Allen, Walter Fuller, and we had so many other trumpet players, man, I can't think of all of them.

Wait a minute, I'm trying -- I'm thinking about the band after we started broadcasting. After we got, you know, made all the changes. Got tight and everything, and started broadcasting. In the trombone section we had Louis Taylor and William Franklin. William Franklin sang and played trombone. In the saxophone section, as I say, we had Darnell Howard, Omer Simeon on lead sax, James Mundy on tenor sax, Cecil Irwin on tenor sax, and I think that was it

in the saxophone section.
George Dixon doubled trumpet and saxophone, baritone sax. So sometimes we had five saxes.
Yeah. That was rare for those days.
Very rare. Did you do a lot of rehearsing?
Yeah, we used to rehearse sometimes, a couple times a week.
Was Earl a good guy to work for?
Yeah, I never had any problems. Yeah.
